evidence.scope: A recorded decision on whether to install the repowise PR bot on this private repository, with the evidence it was taken on; the edge is that nothing is installed, nothing is paid for, and no code changes.
acceptance: What the per-PR page shows is established by looking at one and recorded: record 2 carries the contents of repowise.dev/pr/repowise-dev/repowise/1204, seen without signing in. What a private repository's page shows is recorded as unresolved, because establishing it requires installing the bot on a private repository, which is the decision itself.
A decision is recorded under ## Outcome: declined, in the founder's words at record 3, with the two conditions that would reopen it.
The install-and-verify criterion does not apply: nothing was installed, so there is no bot comment to record, and saying so is the evidence.
SEEN-098's fourth criterion is marked as decided rather than left open: its ticket file and its Blocks section now say declined and point here.
decisions: Declined. Authority: Ruud, 24 September 2026, recorded verbatim at record 3. The grounds are Contents: Read over the whole private tree, repowise's servers cloning the repository to index it, an unresolved question about whether a private repository's per-PR page is public, 15 USD per month before the bot says anything on a private repository, and nothing in the harness depending on it.

Whether a private repository's analysis page is publicly readable is not established and is recorded as not established. Their README lists a public per-PR page with no sign-in as a feature with no carve-out for private repositories, and their /privacy and /security pages both return 404. What would settle it is repowise saying so, or an installation on a throwaway private repository; neither was done, because a decline needs neither.

This ticket is not being reopened by a future maintainer's opinion. Two named conditions reopen it: the repository becoming public, or repowise stating that a private repository's page is access-controlled. Taken by the implementer so that the decision has an expiry rather than becoming folklore.

The ticket is worked in non-code mode with change type policy. It produces a decision and two documentation edits and no executable behaviour, so there is nothing to prove with a test and inventing one would be theatre.
